units_per_mm.basis: No single scale is provable from the record stream alone. Primary reading: 1 raw unit = 0.254 mm (10 mil). Basis: (a) RECORD=31 CustomX/CustomY = 1500 x 950 units then equals exactly 15.00 x 9.50 inch = 381.0 x 241.3 mm, i.e. round inch-based sheet figures; (b) 75 of 85 pins have PinLength=10 units = 100 mil, the most common Altium pin length, and 20 units = 200 mil for the rest; (c) every wire vertex and graphics coordinate is a multiple of 5 units, i.e. a 50 mil entry grid on top of the 100/200 mil component pin pitches; (d) the drawing occupies 209.6 x 118.1 mm against an 82.7 x 57.7 mm board (5.2x board area), a normal schematic-to-board ratio. See sch_extract_notes.md for the ranked alternatives (0.127 mm = 5 mil is the main one) and for the evidence that could not be resolved offline.

alternatives.supporting: Symbol pin pitches then match the physical footprint pad pitches of the same components almost 1:1 (U1 SOP16 1.27 mm pitch drawn at 20 units, D1 2.54 mm part drawn at 20 units) and the designator font size 10 units becomes 1.27 mm, a typical Altium text height.
alternatives.against: The whole schematic drawing (104.8 x 59.1 mm) would be only 1.3x the board area (82.7 x 57.7 mm) for 41 symbols, and the sheet would be smaller than A5, i.e. smaller than any Altium sheet preset.

alternatives.supporting: Sheet and coordinates are simultaneously round in millimetres; the 1500/6 and 950/4 border zone fields give a near-constant 50 mm zone pitch.
alternatives.against: Pin length 2 mm and a 1 mm entry grid are not Altium-typical; 300 x 190 mm matches no ISO preset.
The drawing (82.5 x 46.5 mm) would be smaller than the board area covered, and pin length would be 1 mm; effectively excluded.

units.conversion: millimetres = raw_integer * 0.254 (primary inference); raw integers are always kept in the *_raw fields and in raw_fields. To rescale, multiply the mm values by (new_unit_mm / 0.254).
